newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - French bank boss freed on day six of siege.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - French bank boss freed on day six of siege.

text.p: Hundreds of employees occupying the Paris headquarters of the troubled bank Credit Foncier de France released chairman Jerome Meyssonnier on Wednesday, the sixth day of their siege in a campaign against plans to break up the bank.

Meyssonnier, who had been prevented from leaving since staff started the occupation on Friday, told employees in the building he was "delighted" by a decision which demonstrated their sense of responsbility.

Meyssonnier's declaration followed word from the unions leading the campaign that Mayssonnier and several board members who have been held along with him were no longer being barred from leaving the downtown Paris building.
"We are delighted by this opening, which shows the sense of responsibility of all and everyone and the desire to preserve the image of our company," Meyssonnier said.
The release would help to restart the dialogue on the future of the bank with the help of the government-appointed mediator, Philippe Rouvillois, he added.
Union spokesman Jean-Claude Mabourde told staff just before that the decision to allow Meyssonnier and his board members to leave was a "wise and reasonable" one.

The unions would now call Rouvillois to further press their campaign to keep the bank, which was founded 145 years ago by emperor Napoleon III and has provided cheap home loans to poorer families in France for decades, intact and in business, he said.

Meyssonnier and seven colleagues have been held since Friday in the protest over the government plans to break up the group, spin off part of it to another cooperatively run lender called Credit Immobilier and wind the rest down over time.
